title: Glyph: A Multi-Strategy Agentic System for Column Description and Sensitivity-Ontology Tagging of Enterprise Data Catalogs
gist: Glyph is a production multi-agent LLM system that documents and governance-tags enterprise data-lake columns: a Descriptor agent grounds descriptions in the pipeline source code pulled from an enterprise GitHub via active RAG, and a Tagger runs three parallel strategies fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion against a 275-leaf Data Classification Ontology. A fine-tuned 6-layer MiniLM metadata encoder lifts same-tag retrieval NDCG@10 from 0.55 to 0.92, and the design is deliberately value-free and code-grounded to stay auditable in production.

themes.theme: Documentation debt as a governance risk

insights.claim: Enterprise data lakes accumulate tables faster than human stewards can document or classify them, leaving columns with missing descriptions and unassigned governance labels.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Defines the demand driver for automated cataloging tooling: the backlog is structural and grows with data volume, so manual staffing cannot close it.
insights.quote: Enterprise data lakes accumulate tables faster than human stewards can document or classify them, leaving columns with missing descriptions and unassigned governance labels.
insights.locator: Enterprise data lakes accumulate tables faster

insights.claim: Undocumented and unclassified columns are framed as a 'documentation debt' that simultaneously undermines data discovery, access control, and regulatory compliance.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Links a data-engineering hygiene problem directly to compliance exposure, which is how such tooling gets budget approved.
insights.quote: This documentation debt undermines data discovery, access control, and regulatory compliance.
insights.locator: This documentation debt undermines data discovery

insights.claim: Column description generation and column type annotation for data classification are treated as two coupled problems solved by cooperating LLM agents orchestrated as stateful graphs, rather than as separate pipelines.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A concrete template for agentic architecture in enterprise data infrastructure: stateful graph orchestration over coupled tasks, not single-shot prompting.
insights.quote: frames two coupled problems, column description generation and column type annotation for data classification, as cooperating LLM agents orchestrated as stateful graphs
insights.locator: We present Glyph, a production system

insights.claim: The Descriptor agent grounds each column description in the pipeline source code that produces that column, retrieved on demand from an enterprise GitHub through a reasoning-acting tool loop, i.e. active Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Shows source repositories, not the data itself, becoming the authoritative grounding corpus for data catalogs — raising the strategic value of code-hosting platforms inside the data stack.
insights.quote: The Descriptor grounds generation in the pipeline source code that produces each column, retrieved on demand from an enterprise GitHub via a reasoning–acting tool loop (active Retrieval-Augmented Generation).
insights.locator: The Descriptor grounds generation in the pipeline source code

insights.claim: Glyph is deliberately value-free and code-grounded, meaning it classifies sensitive data without reading actual column values — the key engineering distinction from commercial value/regex sensitivity scanners.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A privacy-preserving classification approach that sidesteps data access entirely; a differentiator to watch as incumbent scanners that sample real values face tightening data-residency rules.
insights.quote: value-free and code-grounded design, per-tag provenance, and graceful degradation
insights.locator: the engineering decisions that distinguish Glyph

insights.claim: Per-tag provenance and graceful degradation are called out as the properties that make multi-agent LLM cataloging auditable and operable as a production service, not just a demo.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Auditability and degradation behaviour, not raw accuracy, are the gating features for enterprise agentic deployments — a useful screen for evaluating vendors.
insights.quote: Together these make multi-agent LLM cataloging auditable and operable as a production service.
insights.locator: Together these make multi-agent LLM cataloging

insights.claim: The Tagger assigns labels from a governed 275-leaf Data Classification Ontology by running three complementary strategies in parallel — a description tagger, a line-of-business regex tagger, and a metadata tagger backed by a fine-tuned contrastive encoder over a vector database — then fuses their ranked outputs with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Evidence that production LLM systems still hedge with classical regex and retrieval ensembles rather than trusting a single model — relevant to how much of the stack an LLM vendor can actually capture.
insights.quote: running three complementary strategies in parallel (a description tagger, a line-of-business regex tagger, and a metadata tagger backed by a fine-tuned contrastive encoder over a vector database), then fuses their ranked outputs with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
insights.locator: The Tagger assigns labels from a governed 275-leaf

insights.claim: Fine-tuning a 6-layer MiniLM metadata encoder with an in-batch contrastive objective lifted same-tag retrieval on an in-distribution held-out split from NDCG@10 of 0.55 to 0.92 and MAP@100 from 0.19 to 0.90 versus the stock base encoder.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A near-5x MAP gain from cheap domain fine-tuning of a tiny 6-layer encoder shows where enterprise ML ROI actually sits — small specialized models, not frontier scale.
insights.quote: lifting same-tag retrieval on an in-distribution held-out split from NDCG@10 0.55 to 0.92 (MAP@100 0.19→ 0.90) relative to the stock base encoder
insights.locator: We fine-tune a 6-layer MiniLM metadata encoder

insights.claim: End-to-end multi-label tagging quality is reported under a recall-weighted F2 objective across three evaluation groups, with an ablation isolating each strategy and the RRF fusion.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The choice of a recall-weighted metric signals that in data governance, missing a sensitive column is far costlier than a false positive — a design constraint buyers should insist on.
insights.quote: We report end-to-end multi-label tagging quality under a recall-weighted F2 objective across three evaluation groups
insights.locator: We report end-to-end multi-label tagging quality

insights.claim: The system is credited to Kostia Kudriavtsev, Parvez Rafi and Sha Sundaram and is filed under the Data Science and Annotation and Privacy research areas, indicating internal enterprise data-governance tooling being surfaced publicly.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Publishing internal data-catalog infrastructure hints at the scale of the underlying data-governance problem and a bias toward privacy-preserving designs.
insights.locator: Authors Kostia Kudriavtsev, Parvez Rafi, Sha Sundaram

insights.claim: Natural language descriptions produced by automated interpretability of LLM features are often vague, inconsistent and require manual relabeling, motivating 'semantic regexes' — structured language descriptions combining linguistic and semantic primitives with contextualizing modifiers.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A caution that free-text interpretability outputs are not reliable audit artifacts yet; structured descriptions are the emerging fix.
insights.quote: these natural language feature descriptions are often vague, inconsistent, and require manual relabeling
